title: Diabetes – Key Facts and Prevention
summary:
Diabetes is a disease where the body can't use sugar properly because it either doesn't make enough insulin or uses what there is wrongly, and this leads to high blood sugar levels called hyperglycaemia. This condition affects many people around the world causing damage mainly in nerves and vessels over time if not managed well. In 2014, about one eighth of adults had diabetes which led to nearly two million deaths directly from it by 2019 with most happening before age seventy-five. Diabetes also causes kidney disease deaths and contributes significantly to heart diseases leading to blindness in some cases too, especially affecting the eyes called retinopathy which can lead to not being able to see well or at all due to diabetes complications worldwide.

Type 2 is most common form of this disease often linked with obesity and lack of exercise while Type 1 happens when pancreas fails in insulin production, mostly affecting children but can also happen later on as adults need their own insulin too. Good control through diet, activity, medication if needed, regular check-ups for complications are key to living with this disease and avoid serious problems like heart attacks or strokes that come along due to it in people who already have the condition.

title: About Influenza (Flu) – Symptoms, Spread, and Prevention
summary:
Flu is an illness caused by germs called influenza viruses that affect our nose, throat, and sometimes lungs. It can make people feel sick from mildly uncomfortable to very severe or even deadly in some cases. Every year around this time, millions of folks get the flu in America alone! Since 2010, it's led to a lot of illnesses and hospital visits each year too.

Flu germs spread when people cough, sneeze or talk near others without covering their mouths. Sometimes they can pick up these germs by touching things that have them on then touch their faces later. Most healthy adults might pass the flu to someone else starting 1 day before feeling sick and for about a week afterward. Kids, especially those under two years old or people with weak immune systems like asthma sufferers, diabetics, heart patients, pregnant women, nursing home residents may get sicker quicker than others when they catch the flu.

People of any age can feel feverish and chills, cough a lot, have aches in muscles or body, headaches, tiredness, runny nose, stuffy nose, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea (more common for kids), but not everyone with flu will get these.

title: High Blood Pressure (Hypertension) – Causes, Risks and Treatment
summary:
High blood pressure, also known as hypertension, often has no noticeable symptoms but can lead to serious problems like heart attacks and strokes if untreated. About a third of UK adults have high blood pressure; many don't know it because there are usually no signs or feelings that something is wrong. The only way to find out your own blood pressure level is by getting checked regularly, especially for those over 40 years old every five years at least.

Blood pressures show two numbers when measured: the systolic number (higher) shows how hard your heart pumps blood around you and diastolic number (lower) represents resistance in vessels to flowing blood, both are recorded as millimetres of mercury or mmHg. High is considered 140/90mmHg or above while ideal pressure ranges between 90/60mmHg and 120/80mmHg; readings from 120/80 to 140/90 could mean you're at risk of developing high blood pressure.
